headline: Nikon disqualified the winner of its microscope video contest because generative AI was used in making the winning entry.
score_reason: Kept at 6: Nikon's own ruling, reported by the BBC, in a public test case for AI-made scientific media; limited to one contest.
importance_line: Scientists and competition organisers are affected because a prize-winning video of a child's airway broke the contest's rules on generative AI, though Nikon says it is not judging the entrant's reputation.
summary: BBC News reports that Nikon has disqualified the winner of its Small World In Motion contest, which accepts video taken through powerful microscopes, saying the use of generative AI broke the rules. The winning video, by Dr Ning Xu of Tsinghua University in China, showed hair-like cilia moving in the airway of a child with the lung condition PCD; scientists said it looked fake, while Xu says he believed he was within the rules.
notes: Full BBC text read. Nikon will also review the contest rules.
